key_insight: ARDY aims to bring high-quality human motion generation into interactive, real-time settings by combining the speed of autoregressive generation with the expressiveness of diffusion models. Its hybrid representation helps preserve controllability while handling complex motion semantics and long-horizon goals.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between offline motion generation methods, which are controllable but too slow for interactive use, and online methods, which are fast but often less controllable and weaker at understanding rich text prompts or long-term motion objectives.
method: Uses an autoregressive diffusion framework to generate motion incrementally for interactive responsiveness.
Introduces a hybrid representation to better balance realism, controllability, and temporal consistency.
Targets complex text-conditioned and long-horizon human motion generation in real time.
impact: This is useful for practitioners building animation tools, simulation systems, and humanoid agents that need both low-latency inference and expressive control. It points toward a practical path for deploying motion generation in interactive environments without sacrificing quality.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing text/goal input flowing into autoregressive diffusion motion generation.
Side-by-side comparison of offline vs online motion generation tradeoffs.
Timeline visualization of long-horizon motion control and rollout.
Icon set for speed, controllability, realism, and context length.
paper_title: ARDY: Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for Interactive Human Motion Generation
paper_authors: Kaifeng Zhao, Mathis Petrovich, Haotian Zhang, Tingwu Wang, Siyu Tang
